cumbia-on-avance.title: Cumbia — moving on
cumbia-on-avance.description: Got the basics? Now we work on dynamics, quick changes, melody and playing "without a net".

cumbia-10-nuances.title: Dynamics: soft down, strong up
cumbia-10-nuances.description: The same continuous down-up motion, but the downstrokes are light (small arrows) and the upstrokes, on the off-beats, are firm. This contrast makes your cumbia come alive, even without changing the pattern.
cumbia-10-nuances.goal: A real loud/soft contrast, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: Downstrokes: just brush 2 strings with the tip of your nail. Upstrokes: all the strings, with more speed.
Exaggerate the contrast at first; you'll refine it later.
Listen to the guide: the small arrows sound almost like a breath.

cumbia-11-majeur.title: Cumbia in C: C – F – G7
cumbia-11-majeur.description: The three most useful chords on the ukulele (I – IV – V), in chucu-chucu. We add F: only two fingers, and it shares the finger on the G string with Am.
cumbia-11-majeur.goal: All three chords in chucu-chucu, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: C → F: lift the finger off the A string and place two fingers (G and E strings). Practice it on its own, without music, 10 times.
Change chords during the chuck (✕): the strings don't ring, so nobody hears the move.
During the G7 bar, already look at where your hand will go for the C.

cumbia-12-demi-mesure.title: Changing every 2 beats
cumbia-12-demi-mesure.description: Am and E7 alternate every two beats in the first bar, then you settle on Am. The changes come twice as fast: this is the step between "I know my chords" and "I play songs".
cumbia-12-demi-mesure.goal: No late changes, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: Am → E7: the finger on the G string moves back one fret (2 → 1) and two fingers are added on fret 2 (C and A strings). Picture this move before you play.
If it's not working, set the starting tempo to 50: speed will come.
Stop looking at your fretting hand: watch the "Next" box on screen instead.

cumbia-13-melodie.title: A melody over Am – G – F – E7
cumbia-13-melodie.description: A short original 4-bar melody that follows the Andalusian progression. Every bar uses the same rhythm ("ta . ta-ta . ta-ta .") but with the notes of the current chord: you hear the melody "draw" the harmony.
cumbia-13-melodie.goal: All 4 bars back to back, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: Learn one bar at a time, with the guide on, muting the rest of the band if needed.
The rhythm is identical in all 4 bars: once it's in your hand, only the frets change.
Reminder: pink = A string, yellow = E, turquoise = C.

cumbia-14-sans-filet.title: Without a net: no guide, no metronome
cumbia-14-sans-filet.description: The guide ukulele and the click are off. Only the band is left, just like at a real dance: it's up to you to lock in with the guiro and the bass. This is what real playing feels like.
cumbia-14-sans-filet.goal: Stay in time for 4 loops at 105 bpm, listening only to the band.
tips: The guiro is your best friend: its long scrape always lands on the beat.
The bass plays on 1 and 3: if you hear it "before" you, you're dragging.
To make it harder: turn on the silence challenge.
